title: Global Temperature Anomalies (1880–Present)
audioLegend: Audio Legend: Deep bass notes mean cooler historical temperatures. Rising high chimes mean extreme global warming.

milestones.text: 1980: Warming trend accelerates across the Northern Hemisphere.
Present day: Record-breaking global heat anomalies.

title: Global Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Plumes
audioLegend: Audio Legend: Sound pans from left to right as carbon plumes travel eastward. Higher pitch means higher carbon concentration.

milestones.text: Northern spring: Carbon dioxide builds over major industrial zones.
Summer: Vegetation absorbs carbon, lowering the musical pitch.
Winter: Emissions rise again and swirl across the globe.

title: Arctic Sea Ice Minimum
audioLegend: Audio Legend: Low, grounded tones represent thick sea ice. As white ice shrinks, the pitch rises to signal ice loss.

milestones.text: 1984: Thick multi-year sea ice covers the Arctic Ocean.
2012: Historic minimum sea ice extent recorded.
Present day: Younger, thinner seasonal ice remains.
